newsitem.title: USA: Lehman should have checked Centennial trades - SEC.
newsitem.headline: Lehman should have checked Centennial trades - SEC.

text.p: Lehman Brothers had an obligation to check the "overwhelming" suspicious circumstances when a former Centennial Technologies Inc Chief Executive traded options on his company, a lawyer for the Securities and Exchange Commission said Thursday.

Lehman's suspicions should have been raised when former Centennial Chief Executive Emanuel Pinez asked to trade more than 4,300 options on the company within a few hours on Feb. 7, the SEC lawyer Jeffrey Kobrick told a U.S. District Court.

Pinez has been jailed since last month when the SEC charged him with insider trading and fradulently manipulating Centennial's sales figures. Through his lawyer, he has denied committing any wrongdoing.
Lehman stood to gain by executing the trade, Kobrick said, and thus it was in the company's interest not to stop the trade.
"This is an outrageous situation," Kobrick said. "It's a highly self-interested transaction," he added.
Robert Gad, representing Lehman, said there is no evidence Lehman did anything wrong and it had no duty to make inquiries into the trade.
He said the number of options was not of an unusual size considering that Pinez owned hundreds of thousands of Centennial shares.

Lehman was owed about $5.4 million by Pinez when his account was frozen and Chicago options market makers claim to be out more than $3.75 million. Both parties have laid claim to the assets in Pinez's brokerage account, which the court ordered frozen with the proceeds held in escrow.
"There are two kinds of people here and one of them is going to get stuck," Gad said. "We have someone who is going to get hurt for $4 million."
